title.narrative: Strengthened Accountability for Torture and related violations through enhanced investigative, judicial, penal and reparative mechanisms

description.narrative: The Independent Medical Legal Unit (IMLU) is a governance, health, and human rights non-governmental organization with a vision of having A Society free from Torture and Related Violations. Our work is fostered by a holistic approach that includes litigation, medical and psycho-social rehabilitation, socio-economic empowerment, oversight of government compliance with human rights obligations, and advocacy of political, legal, and institutional reforms that promote accountability, healing, and justice. Over the last three decades, the organization has supported more than 6,000 victims of torture, and cruel, degrading, and inhumane treatments. We have a national presence of over 300 professionals; doctors, trauma counsellors, lawyers, human rights monitors, and journalists.

activity-date.narrative: Within the period under review, IMLU engaged with various stakeholders in the justice sector to harness partnerships and collaborations that will ensure duty bearers respond to cases of torture and related violations to ensure healing and justice for victims and survivors. This was carried out through engagements on full implementation of POTA and the National Coroner Services Act (NCSA) of 2017. On POTA, IMLU held consultative forums with ODPP, DCI and the Judiciary on policing accountability through activation of charges under the Act as opposed to charging police officers under the Penal Code. A committee was formed known as the Tripartite that would oversee training of investigating officers at the DCI, IPOA, IAU and the ODPP on drafting charge sheets under POTA. Similarly, IMLU engaged in consultation with the Department of Justice on the need to review NCSA 2017 to support its implementation. The administrative functions of the Act placed the Cabinet Secretary for Justice, an office that does not exist in the republic had hindered its operationalization. To this end, the DoJ published the NCS Amendment Bill 2023 to rectify this anomaly. The Bill is set to go through the legal process for review in 2024. In order to develop and support the government in reporting on the UNCAT, IMLU convened a UPR thematic group meeting on Torture, Enforced Disappearance and Death Penalty. The forum took stock of the current development and the need to review the alternative report prepared in the 3rd cycle for sharing during the 4th Cycle of the UPR in October 2024. In 2024, Gen-Z led protested the passing of the Finance Act that would otherwise worsen the cost of living for many Kenyans. These protests highlighted the intersection of economic policy and the human rights landscape in the Country. In 2025, the protests were also witnessed across the country especially in June during the commemoration of the lives lost in June 2024. Unfortunately, state responses to these protests was characterized by violent crackdowns by the security personnel, police brutality, including enforced disappearance, torture and extrajudicial killings, demonstrating the governmentâ€™s prioritization of control over addressing the legitimate grievances of its citizens.

title.narrative: Public trust and confidence in the justice sector through cooperative dialogue with the citizens

description.narrative: The mothers of victims have approached different government entities to demand for timely rehabilitation services such as the Medical, psychological and Socio-economic empowerment. Members of the social justice centres, mostly youth, in Kondele have demanded the NPS respects the right to life and put a stop to the cycle of human rights violations.

comment.narrative: More officers from the NPS attended the training on Forensic documentation and the training on sexual and gender-based violence. With increased demand for training among the state officers, IMLU will consider revising the targets in the next reporting period.

title.narrative: # of coordination forums held between different security and justice actors

comment.narrative: Police reforms were a priority as the President had just received the Maraga task force report at the end of 2023. As such, there was a need to strategize, internalize and plan for the implementation of the recommendations from the report. IMLU in collaboration with PRWG-K and MoI held 4 forums leading to the national policing forum. 3 other forums were held with the Prisons Reforms Working Group leading to the penal reforms symposium and 2 forums leading to the PRWG-K strategic workshop. The meeting with Parliamentarians did not happen due to the demand for allowances that is higher than the IMLU rate.

comment.narrative: The laws in place include the National Coroners Service Act (NCSA) and The Prevention of Torture Act (POTA)

IMLU through the police reforms working group has proposed the development of the National Policing Law, the National Police Service Act, IPOA Act. The proposed laws are yet to be formulated and adopted for discussion by different stakeholders, including parliament. Discussion for the formulation of a Victims Protection fund is underway.
